A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoLA and CoLA-M. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original CoLA pre-training, GLUE evaluation, activation-spectrum analysis, ablations, and system measurements, although some baseline results are attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds BERT configuration comparisons and revised activation-spectrum results.

M1.justification: CoLA’s auto-encoder replacement and CoLA-M’s checkpointing procedure remain unchanged. v3 discloses the gated BERT implementation behind retained results and evaluates the already-described option of preserving original nonlinearities; this does not establish a new core method.

E1.justification: Both versions use C4, Wikipedia, WikiText2, and the same GLUE tasks. The additional BERT configurations and spectral diagnostics remain within existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained in the matched pre-training, scaling, GLUE, and system comparisons. New Table 10 compares CoLA configurations against the existing BERTLarge baseline; it adds an ablation rather than a new baseline method.

E3.justification: v3 adds BERT controls varying MLP gating and preservation of the original activation, including a 128-token phase-one diagnostic. Figure 2 is corrected to explicitly measure post-nonlinearity activations. Existing headline training budgets, metrics, and profiling procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2 adds a targeted BERT analysis separating CoLA’s effect from MLP gating and examines failure when removing the original activation from an ungated MLP. Spectral diagnostics are revised and expanded. The existing LLaMA activation-placement ablation is retained as Table 11.

E5.justification: GLUE results continue to report the mean of the best five of ten random seeds, including the added configuration. No new empirical confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting procedures appear. The new probabilistic theoretical bound belongs under T1.

E6.justification: New Table 10 reports loss 1.265 and GLUE average 83.5 for CoLA with the original BERT MLP, alongside the retained gated configuration’s 1.257 and 83.5. Appendix D.2 adds the phase-one loss comparison 1.579 versus 1.403, and activation spectra change. Matched main benchmark and system results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Section 3.3 introduces two propositions and two theorems covering nonlinear representational capacity, sufficient conditions for strict superiority over linear low-rank approximation, and an effective-rank-aware recovery bound. Appendices G–H add proofs and four auxiliary lemmas. v2 contained rank definitions and resource-cost derivations but lacked this theory.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a distinct theoretical contribution: conditional strict superiority over conventional low-rank models and a non-asymptotic recovery bound sensitive to spectral concentration. This substantially expands the claimed contributions beyond v2’s architectural, empirical, and system-efficiency contributions, whose headline claims are retained.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands the mechanism explanation through nonlinear features outside the input row space and discusses the recovery bound’s dependence on spectral concentration. It explicitly limits theoretical coverage of MLP layers and explains the ungated-BERT activation-removal failure, with remedies and a preference for gating. These qualifications were absent from v2.

D1.justification: Appendix D.2 newly identifies gating as part of the implementation behind the retained BERT results and documents the alternative activation-preserving configuration. The code link changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository. Appendix A removes the previously stated spectral-analysis batch size of 64 without specifying a replacement.

R1.justification: v3 adds Vershynin’s High-Dimensional Probability to support the recovery proof. Section 2 also refines CompAct’s positioning concerning computation relative to GaLore and accuracy relative to GaLore and full-rank training. The broader related-work coverage remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose edits, clarifies MLP versus projection-layer terminology, adds authors and contact information, and integrates a theoretical subsection and proof appendices. The existing narrative is largely retained; the added scientific content does not amount to extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the activation-spectrum plots, clarifies their captions, adds Figure 12 distinguishing MLP-block output, and adds the BERT comparison table. The memory-analysis table moves from main-text Table 4 to Appendix C’s Table 9. Other architecture and system figures retain their displays despite layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important gaps in justification and experimental attribution: Section 3.3 and Appendices G–H add conditional theory and proofs, while Appendix D.2 discloses the previously unspecified BERT gating change and supplies an original-MLP control that still achieves 83.5 GLUE versus BERTLarge’s 82.7. Corrected spectral displays further strengthen the motivation. The theory remains conditional and only partly covers MLP layers, and the spectral batch-size disclosure is lost, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in explanation, transparency, and supporting evidence.
